title: Rescaling and clearing denominators before forming the delocalized quotient
statement: Let $R,A,\Lambda$ be commutative rings, with $A$ and $\Lambda$ algebras over $R$, and let $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ be an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Let $S\subset R$ be a multiplicative submonoid and use localization at its images [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Fix nonnegative integers $n,t,m,c$ with $c\le n+m$, and a presentation $P$ of $A$ with generators $p_i$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}n$), relations $g_j\in R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1}]$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}t$), and kernel generated by these relations [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $D$ be an $S^{-1}R$-algebra, $Q$ a standard smooth presentation of $D$ with $n+m$ variables and $c$ relations whose initial Jacobian minor is a unit [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and $S^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\beta}D\xrightarrow{\gamma}S^{-1}\Lambda$ a factorization of $S^{-1}\alpha$. Suppose that the first $n$ variables of $Q$ represent $\beta(p_i/1)$. Put $T=R[x_0,\ldots,x_{n+m-1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], write $\widetilde g_j$ for $g_j$ with variables included as the first $n$, and use polynomial partial derivatives [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Then there exist polynomials $f_j\in T$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}c$), elements $l_i\in\Lambda$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+m)$), $s_0\in S$, $a_0,a_j\in T$, and $sg_j\in S$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}t$), $sf_j\in S$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}c$), such that $l_i=\alpha(p_i)$ for $i<n$, $C(s_0)=a_0\Delta(f)+\sum_{j<c}a_jf_j$, $C(sg_j)\widetilde g_j\in(f_0,\ldots,f_{c-1})$ for every $j<t$, and $\operatorname{ev}_l(C(sf_j)f_j)=0$ for every $j<c$. Here $C:R\to T$ is the constant inclusion and $\Delta(f)=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j<c}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof

proof.text: Write gamma(Q.val_i)=l_i/d_i for extra indices, with d_i in S, and put d_i=1, l_i=alpha(P.val_i) for the first n using hfactor and hval. Replace the generators by d_i Q.val_i and substitute X_i/d_i in the old relations. Substitution by d_i X_i is its inverse. The chain rule scales each selected Jacobian row by d_i inverse, a unit, so the new minor remains invertible.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof, rescaling the variables

proof.text: Identify the localized polynomial ring with localization of T, using polynomial scalar extension and localization base change. Multiply each equation by a denominator of its coefficients to obtain f_j in T. These multipliers are units after localization, so they preserve the relation ideal and the invertibility of the minor.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof, clearing equation coefficients

proof.text: Lift the inverse minor to K[X] by surjectivity, and express the error using the relations. Obtain 1=b_0 Delta(f)+sum b_j f_j in K[X]. Clear all b_j coefficient denominators by d in S to give polynomial a_j. The difference C(d)-a_0 Delta(f)-sum a_j f_j maps to zero in K[X]. The polynomial-localization kernel criterion supplies e in S annihilating that difference. Multiply all a_j by C(e) and take s_0=e*d, obtaining the exact identity in T without assuming localization injective.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof, the identity involving s_0

proof.text: Each renamed original relation g_j vanishes in the localized quotient, because its first variables represent beta(p_i/1). Express it in the localized equation ideal, clear coefficients and the equality, giving sg_j in S with C(sg_j) g_j in (f).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base), proof, choosing s_j

proof.text: The rescaled variables map under gamma to l_i/1, with l_i=alpha(p_i) for the first n. By the factorization identity, evaluating each f_j at these l_i gives zero after localization. The localization kernel criterion supplies sf_j in S killing its evaluation before localization.
